<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par51 />{{center|Verba Derivativa, or Derived Conjugations.}}

<!-- section begins above -->{{GHGpar-heading|51|Niphʿal||<ref>Cf. A. Rieder, ''De linguae Hebr. verbis, quae vocantur derivata nifal et hitpael'', Gumbinnen (Progr. des Gymn.), 1884, a list of all the strong Niphʿal forms (81) and Hithpaʿēl forms (36) in the Old Testament; and especially M. Lambert, ‘L’emploi du Nifal en Hébreu,’ {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|REJ.|Revue des Études Juives. Paris, 1880 ff.}}}} 41, 196 ff.</ref>}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|51|a}}
'''1.''' The essential characteristic of this conjugation consists in a prefix<ref>See Philippi in {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} 1886, p. 650, and Barth, ibid. 1894, p. 8 f.</ref> to the stem. This exists in two forms: (''a'') the (probably original) prepositive ''nă'', as in the Hebrew perfect and participle, although in the strong verb the ''ă'' is always attenuated to ''ĭ'': {{GHGheb|text=נִקְטַל}} for original ''nă-qăṭăl'', participle {{GHGheb|text=נִקְטָל}}, infinitive absolute sometimes {{GHGheb|text=נִקְטוֹל}}; (''b'') the (later) proclitic ''in'' (as in all the forms of the corresponding Arabic conjugation vii. ''ʾinqătălă''), found in the imperfect {{GHGheb|text=יִקָּטֵל}} for ''yinqāṭēl'', in the imperative and infinitive construct, with a secondary {{GHGheb|text=ה}} added, {{GHGheb|text=הִקָּטֵל}} (for ''hinqāṭēl''), and in the infinitive absolute {{GHGheb|text=הִקָּטֹל}} The inflexion of {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} is perfectly analogous to that of Qal.

{{GHGmargin-letter|51|b}}
The features of {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} are accordingly in the perfect and participle the prefixed ''Nûn'', in the imperative, infinitive, and imperfect, the {{GHGterm|Dageš}} in the first radical. These characteristics hold good also for the weak verb. In the case of an initial guttural, which, according to {{GHGpar|22|b}}, cannot take {{GHGterm|Dageš forte}}, the emission of the strengthening invariably causes the lengthening of the preceding vowel (see {{GHGpar|63|h}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|51|c}}
'''2.''' As regards its meaning, {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} bears some resemblance to the Greek ''middle voice'', in being—(''a'') primarily {{GHGterm|reflexive}} of Qal, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=נִלְחַץ|translate=to thrust oneself}} (''against''), {{GHGheb|text=נִשְׁמַר|translate=to take heed to oneself}}, φυλάσσεσθαι, {{GHGheb|text=נִסְתַּר|translate=to hide oneself}}, {{GHGheb|text=נִגְאַל|translate=to redeem oneself}}; cf. also {{GHGheb|text=נַֽעֲנֶה|translate=to answer for oneself}}. Equally characteristic of {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} is its frequent use to express emotions which react upon the mind; {{GHGheb|text=נִחַם|translate=to trouble oneself}}, {{GHGheb|text=נֶֽאֱנַח|translate=to sigh}} (''to bemoan oneself'', cf. ὀδύρεσθαι, ''lamentari, contristari''); as well as to express actions which the subject allows to happen to himself, or to have an effect upon himself (''Niphʿal tolerativum''), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=דָּרַשׁ|translate=to search, to inquire}}, Niph. ''to allow oneself to be inquired of'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=65|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=14|verse=3}}, &c.; so the Niph. of {{GHGheb|text=מָצָא|translate=to find}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָסַר|translate=to warn, to correct}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=6|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=31|verse=18|hidebook=1}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|51|d}}
(''b'') It expresses ''reciprocal'' or mutual action, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=דִּבֶּר|translate=to speak}}, Niph. ''to speak to one another''; {{GHGheb|text=שָׁפַט|translate=to judge}}, Niph. ''to go to law with one another''; {{GHGheb|text=יָעַץ|translate=to counsel}}, Niph. ''to take counsel'', cf. the ''middle'' and ''deponent'' verbs βουλεύεσθαι ({{GHGheb|text=נוֹעַץ}}), μάξεσθαι ({{GHGheb|text=נְלְחַם}}), ''altercari, luctari'' ({{GHGheb|text=נִצָּה|translate=to strive with one another}}) ''proeliari''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|51|e}}
(''c'') It has also, like {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} ({{GHGpar|54|f}}) and the Greek ''middle'', the meaning of the active, with the addition of ''to oneself'' (''sibi''), ''for {{hyphenated word start|one|oneself}}''<section end=par51 /><noinclude>
